key_insight: Aligning a network’s initial representational geometry to a different architecture can transfer optimization benefits without transferring learned features.
engineering_relevance: Initialization alignment may improve shallow or coarse-resolution networks without changing their physical architecture.
method: Use a randomly initialized guide network from a different architecture.
Align the target network’s representational geometry to the guide before downstream training, without labels or guide updates.
Train the aligned target network on the downstream task.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved downstream performance when shallow networks are aligned to deeper guides and coarse-resolution networks to fine-resolution guides, but provides no datasets or numerical results.
watch_item: Alignment adds a preprocessing step whose computational cost and sensitivity to guide selection are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
